newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher in quiet trading as a new 10-year guilder bond by Dutch banking and insurance ING Groep NV and events elswhere captured attention.
Dutch state loans finished in positive territory after a late rally which coincided with renewed strength in German Bund and U.S. Treasury futures.
Dealers instead focussed on the 700 million guilder 6.00 percent May 30, 2007 bond announced by lead manager ING Barings, which was issued at 47 basis points over the government curve.
They described it as a "flyer", narrowing in spread by at least three basis points in secondary market trading.
"Big parties were all in for about five million (guilders)," said one trader.
But the issue had no impact on state paper, they said.
One dealer said the Dutch market was overshadowed by events in Britain, where the new Labour government lifted interest rates and made the Bank of England operationally independent.
He also noted buying interest in shorter Dutch paper, including the July 1998s, which were seen as cheap compared with German paper, which now trades at a yield discount.
Another dealer reported lengthening trades, with sellers of 2005 Dutch bonds swapping into the 2006 area.
